threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Flawed key generation let anyone recover eMudhra intermediate CA keys, exposing TLS clients that skip CT checks
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. Six are for TLS and chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs, and two are for codesigning and trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of these keys could issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate any website or service, and many non-browser clients that do not enforce Certificate Transparency, including curl, are at greater risk.

items.lead: Formal proofs of security properties now reach real libraries at scale, not just toy code.
items.body: Anthropic showed Claude proving security properties across more than 100 open-source libraries in weeks. That puts formal verification within reach of an ordinary security or quality budget. It covers only certain bug classes, and there is no runnable tool to try yet.

items.lead: Skills written for one agent platform now have a vendor-neutral home.
items.body: Agent Skills, already integrated by more than 70 platforms, is now run by the Agentic AI Foundation rather than by Anthropic alone. For builders and buyers worried about lock-in, writing a skill once becomes a safer bet. This changes who governs the standard, not what it can do.

items.lead: Running agents on your own hardware got more practical on several fronts.
items.body: MiniMax M3.1 Flash is an open image-and-text model that SGLang serves at over 1,000 tokens per second single-stream. NVIDIA's Apache-2.0 OpenShell gives teams a shared runtime for agent fleets, so they need not build their own isolation layer. Community tests now show Flint holding 152 tokens per second at 32K context on one RTX 5090. The speed figures come from single setups or the serving project itself, and OpenShell's safety claims are its own.
